reasons.quote: During a business trip, Larkfield reimburses meals at their actual cost up to these limits per meal: breakfast EUR 15, lunch EUR 25, dinner EUR 45. Limits apply to the employee's own meal.
reasons.explanation: This is a solo dinner on a Hamburg business trip. The receipt total is EUR 62.00, which exceeds the EUR 45 dinner limit by EUR 17.00.

reasons.quote: A claim that exceeds a limit in this policy is rejected as a whole. The employee may submit it again with the amount within the limit, explaining the difference in the business purpose.
reasons.explanation: Because the EUR 62.00 total exceeds the EUR 45 dinner limit, the claim must be rejected in full. The employee may resubmit claiming EUR 45 and explaining the difference.

reasons.quote: A meal with clients or partners is reimbursed up to EUR 80 per attendee, counting every attendee including Larkfield employees. The claim must list the names and companies of all attendees and the business purpose of the meeting.
reasons.explanation: The claim lists all 3 attendees (1 Larkfield, 2 Meridian Health) with their companies and states a clear business purpose (Q4 renewal). EUR 240.00 ÷ 3 attendees = EUR 80.00 per attendee, exactly at the limit.

reasons.quote: Alcohol is reimbursed only as part of client entertainment under clause 2.2, and within its per-attendee limit.
reasons.explanation: The two bottles of Barolo (EUR 84.00) are part of a client entertainment dinner under 2.2, and the full bill including alcohol remains within the EUR 80 per attendee limit.

reasons.quote: The claim must list the names and companies of all attendees and the business purpose of the meeting. A client entertainment claim without the attendee list cannot be assessed against the limit.
reasons.explanation: The attendee list is entirely absent. With a total of EUR 190.00, the per-attendee limit of EUR 80 cannot be verified without knowing the full number of attendees and their details.

reasons.quote: When a claim is missing information the employee can provide (attendee list, business purpose, pre-approval reference, an itemised receipt), the reviewer asks for it instead of rejecting.

reasons.explanation: Berlin is not a high-cost city, so the EUR 150 per night limit applies. Both nights are billed at EUR 145.00 each, which is within the limit, and the total of EUR 290.00 for two nights is fully reimbursable.

reasons.explanation: The claim is supported only by a card slip showing a total of EUR 40.00, which exceeds the EUR 25 threshold. An itemised receipt showing the vendor name, date, each item purchased, the total, and the tax amount is required.

reasons.quote: A taxi or ride-hailing trip is reimbursed when public transport is not a reasonable option: when carrying equipment, when no public transport runs, or when the trip starts between 22:00 and 06:00. The limit is EUR 60 per trip.
reasons.explanation: The receipt shows the trip started at 23:30, which falls within the 22:00–06:00 window, making public transport not a reasonable option. The total of EUR 38.00 is within the EUR 60 per-trip limit.

reasons.quote: A taxi or ride-hailing trip is reimbursed when public transport is not a reasonable option: when carrying equipment, when no public transport runs, or when the trip starts between 22:00 and 06:00. The limit is EUR 60 per trip.
reasons.explanation: The trip departed at 14:00, which is outside the 22:00–06:00 night window. The claim does not state that equipment was being carried or that no public transport was available, so none of the three qualifying conditions are met. Additionally, the total of EUR 75.00 exceeds the EUR 60 per-trip limit.

reasons.quote: A claim that exceeds a limit in this policy is rejected as a whole. The employee may submit it again with the amount within the limit, explaining the difference in the business purpose.
reasons.explanation: Even if a qualifying condition were established, the EUR 75.00 charge exceeds the EUR 60 per-trip limit set by clause 3.3, requiring rejection of the claim in full.

reasons.quote: Flights are booked in economy class. Premium economy is allowed for flights over 6 hours. Business and first class are not reimbursed. Flights should be booked at least 14 days before departure; a later booking is allowed when the trip itself was arranged at short notice, and the business purpose says so.
reasons.explanation: The flight is booked in economy class (fare class Y) and was invoiced on 10 June 2026 for a 2 July 2026 departure — 22 days in advance, satisfying the 14-day advance booking requirement.

reasons.quote: Larkfield reimburses reasonable costs that an employee pays personally while doing their job.
reasons.explanation: EUR 210 (fare EUR 158 + taxes/fees EUR 52) for a Frankfurt–Lisbon economy flight is a reasonable cost for attending the Atlas client workshop.

reasons.quote: Business and first class are not reimbursed.
reasons.explanation: The invoice clearly shows the flight was booked in Business class (fare class J) on a 1h 20m Frankfurt–Vienna route. Business class is categorically not reimbursable under clause 3.1, regardless of the route length or purpose.

reasons.quote: A claim that exceeds a limit in this policy is rejected as a whole. The employee may submit it again with the amount within the limit, explaining the difference in the business purpose.
reasons.explanation: Because the business class fare is not reimbursable under 3.1, the entire claim of EUR 890.00 must be rejected. The employee may rebook or resubmit in economy class with the corresponding economy fare and receipt.

Clause 4.2 explicitly prohibits reimbursement of personally purchased software, even when used for work; the employee should ask IT to procure the tool through the company account instead.

This is explicitly a parking ticket and therefore falls squarely within the category of expenses that are never reimbursed under clause 6.1, regardless of the fact that it was incurred during a client visit.

reasons.quote: Minibar, in-room entertainment, spa and laundry are personal expenses.
